newsitem.title: UK: MEPC would consider Hammerson offer-paper.
newsitem.headline: MEPC would consider Hammerson offer-paper.

text.p: British property company MEPC Plc is open to considering bid proposals from its smaller rival Hammerson Plc in spite of merger talks having broken up without agreement, the Times said on Monday.

The report said MEPC chief executive James Tuckey "has indicated that he would consider seriously any offer put to him by Hammerson". It said no concrete proposals had been put by Hammerson in talks which fell apart a few days ago.
No spokesman for MEPC or Hammerson was available for comment on Monday, a public holiday in Britain.

The Sunday Telegraph said MEPC had rejected a proposal of a 3.2 billion pounds merger from Hammerson and was now waiting to see whether Hammerson chief executive Ron Spinney had the courage to mount a hostile bid.

The Times, however, said it was considered unlikely that Hammerson, which at 1.24 billion pounds is capitalised at little more than half the 2.0 billion at which the market values MEPC, that Hammerson would put forward an aggressive offer.
Newspaper reports say that pension fund manager PDFM, which controls a stake of more than 17 percent in each company, would apply pressure for a merger.
The two groups combined would form Britain's second largest property company behind Land Securities Plc, and would be a consituent of the FTSE 100 index.
